newsitem.title: ITALY: New directive grates on Italian cheese makers.
newsitem.headline: New directive grates on Italian cheese makers.

text.p: Italy's antitrust authority on Wednesday gave producers of parmesan cheese three months in which to bring their production practices in line with fair competition objectives.

The watchdog, concluding a year-long inquiry into two consortiums of cheese producers, said changes already introduced by both groups did not go far enough to make their practices conform to a system of fair competition.

There are 600 companies grouped in the consortium of producers of Parmigiano Reggiano and 300 in the consortium producing Grana Padana, which are both hard white cheeses known outside Italy as parmesan and grated on to pasta dishes.

The industry ministry requested the antitrust inquiry more than a year ago after a prices watchdog body noted a year on year rise in March 1995 of 23 percent in the cost of the cheese when production had actually dropped by around 15 percent.
The antitrust body said it found production plans and self-regulation carried out by both consortiums between 1991 and 1995 constituted accords restricting competition.
Together, the two consortiums of Parmigiano Reggiano and Grana Padana produce more than 90 percent of Italy's parmesan cheese. Latest figures put total annual consumption in Italy at 208,400 tonnes.
